lease_API_proposal.B_resource_owner: Existing guest_memory_lease_context embedded in session and associated through existing compat_host_context. Remove provider context/read/write fields; retain eight slots, epoch, active and copy_lock.

operations.contract: Begin activates resource epoch without registering provider callbacks. End holds existing exclusive copy lock, clears buffers and deactivates. F retains lifecycle/admission timing.

Validate context/access/range and reserve existing slot/buffer. No C access. C hydrates all nonempty buffers including WRITE-only; on failure cancel reservation, publish no output. Do not claim early active-slot publication equivalent until reentry boundary is verified.
Check pointer membership before dereference; reject foreign/inactive/stale lease. Return the existing slot only within caller-owned lifetime; no second token registry.
Release and clear validated slot without machine access. C performs conditional commit first and consumes even after failed write; return original write result.
Hold existing shared copy_lock across C read/write with matching active epoch; end waits on exclusive lock. Copy-only access uses no borrowed slot. No callback supplied to B.

lease_API_proposal.C_coordinator: Existing checked provider boundary in ccpusas4.c is the candidate. It must own hydration/commit/short copied access and machine-dependent location operations, calling B resource primitives. Candidate mirror size and original-carrier suitability require measurement/approval before production edits.
lease_API_proposal.F_changes: session_guest_memory_begin removes provider parameters; explicit-owner acquire/release retain ACTIVE admission and call C coordinator. mvdm_softpc_guest_memory_begin installer loses C callback installation. Saved DOSWOW epoch calls use C copied access within B lock scope.
lease_API_proposal.compatibility: Keep existing public mvdm_softpc_guest_memory_* and location access names where feasible, but remove their B implementations which call C callbacks. Two scalar location constructors remain independent. No second session/TLS, no runtime F callbacks in B.
